metadata.note: Original scenario-based learning checks, internally checked against MDN primary documentation; not independently reviewed.

questions.prompt: An app receives HTTP 202 for a queued task. Which message best describes what the app actually knows?
options: The task was accepted but its completion is not yet known
The server has proved the final result
questions.funFact: HTTP 202 acknowledges acceptance for processing. It does not certify the later outcome.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A public data service returns HTTP 503. What should its consumer report about a balance it could not read?
questions.funFact: HTTP 503 indicates that a service is currently unable to handle the request. An unavailable read does not establish the underlying value.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A service responds HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Which response respects the service limit?
options: Wait for the indicated interval before retrying
Treat the response as a confirmed payment
questions.funFact: HTTP 429 reports too many requests. Retry-After can communicate how long the client should wait.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A browser aborts a fetch request after a timeout. Which conclusion about a remote write is justified?
options: The browser stopped waiting; the remote outcome may still need checking
The server certainly rolled back the write
questions.funFact: Aborting cancels the client fetch operation. That client-side action is not evidence that a remote application reversed an earlier write.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP method is defined for retrieving a representation rather than asking the server to change application state?
questions.funFact: GET requests a representation and is defined as a safe method. Sensitive information and write operations still need appropriate handling.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A learner saves preferences in localStorage. What lifetime should the app normally expect for those values?
options: They persist across browser sessions until removed or storage is cleared
They are automatically shared with every device
questions.funFact: localStorage is scoped to an origin and persists across browser sessions. It is not a substitute for backups and can be unavailable or cleared.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A result receipt uses sessionStorage. Which description best matches the browser feature?
options: Storage tied to the page origin and the current tab session
A public record visible to all users
A shared database across all devices
questions.funFact: sessionStorage is partitioned by origin and top-level browsing context. Closing a tab or window ends that page session.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: An iPhone browser refuses an automatic Copy action. What user interface should preserve access to the text?
options: A selectable text field for manual copying
A request for a wallet seed phrase
questions.funFact: Clipboard access is restricted and browser permission behavior varies. A manual-copy path gives the user another way to obtain the text.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: What does the HttpOnly cookie attribute prevent in ordinary page scripts?
questions.funFact: HttpOnly prevents JavaScript access through document.cookie. It is one control and does not replace request-origin or authorization checks.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: Why should an app catch localStorage write errors instead of assuming every Save action worked?
options: Browser policy or storage limits can prevent the write
Every write creates a verified cloud backup
Saving a preference broadcasts a transaction
questions.funFact: Access can raise SecurityError when persistence is disallowed. Apps should handle unavailable storage and avoid promising that a record was saved.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A counter exceeds JavaScript Number safe-integer precision. Which representation can preserve its integer value?
options: BigInt or a validated decimal string
questions.funFact: BigInt represents integers beyond Number safe-integer limits. Display formatting and external JSON representation are separate concerns.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript check tests whether a Number value is an exactly representable safe integer?
questions.funFact: Number.isSafeInteger rejects fractions, non-number values and integers outside the safe-integer range.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A response body contains broken JSON syntax. What should a caller expect from JSON.parse?
options: A SyntaxError rather than a reliable parsed result
questions.funFact: JSON.parse parses JSON text and throws SyntaxError for invalid syntax. Applications should handle that failure explicitly.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: A JSON counter arrives as the string "120". Which statement describes its initial JavaScript type?
options: It is a string until explicitly interpreted or converted
It is automatically a validated address
questions.funFact: Strings hold text. A decimal-looking string requires separate validation before it is used as a numeric counter.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.

questions.prompt: What is the result of comparing the Number 120 and the string "120" with JavaScript strict equality?
options: False because the operand types differ
True because the characters look similar
questions.funFact: Strict equality does not convert different operand types to a common type. Number and string operands are different types.
questions.attribution: Original questions by Geek Protocol; factual references linked individually.
